summary: Idaho cab on Stormy Peak, built in 1928 after a 1920 tent camp; lost in the Moose Fire in July 2022. Sources disagree on the cab's design.

facts.design: Modified L-4 cab on a log base (register); other sources describe a two-story base with an R-4 cab
facts.status_note: Lost in the Moose Fire, reported July 25, 2022. No source we read describes what, if anything, remains.

access.note: Hike-in site on national forest land. The 2022 report describes poor trail access. No closure is reported in our sources.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in with poor trail access, per the 2022 report. The lookout burned in 2022, so there is no structure to climb.

events.note: Tent camp activated on the site; the 1928 cab replaced it, per the register.
Register says built on the Salmon-Challis National Forest in 1928. firelookout.com also gives 1928. Design described differently by each source.
1935 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page: Pete Burton left for the lookout.
High frequency radio installed at the lookout, per a 1950 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page.
1951 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page: Oscar Schmunk and his wife stationed on the peak.
1956 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page: Al Clary manned the lookout; he and his wife planted a vegetable garden.
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Susan Hunter as known staff for 1977 to 1978.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on September 24, 2011.
Moose Fire. The register says the lookout was reported lost on July 25, 2022.
Lost to the Moose Fire. Logbook and fire finder were removed the day before; the lookout was not wrapped or protected by sprinklers. Radio repeater lost too, per a local news report.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com both give 1928 for the cab. The camp date is 1920 in the register and the Forest Lookouts page, and 1920s in the Idaho Fire Lookouts timeline.

sources.title: Moose Fire burns lookout building and radio tower

notes_for_editor: Design conflict is unresolved. The register says a modified L-4 cab on a one-story log base, which matches the record's design L-4. The record's kind two_story matches the Forest Lookouts page, Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com, which say two-story, but the register says one-story. Not proposed as a correction; a human should check the 1928 build against a Forest Service or a photo. Forest name: the register says Salmon-Challis National Forest; firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page say Salmon National Forest (the older name). Staff items come from newspaper quotes on a fan site and from Idaho Fire Lookouts, not checked against the original papers. Access level 'public' is inferred from national forest land and the hike-in label; no closure notice was found. Not read: a Forest Service Moose Fire update on Facebook and a groups.io post, both in search results. The 2022 chapter report includes a personal 2009 visit by its author; not used.
